descriptionChirho: Qal intransitive sense: to come to ruin, perish, die, cease to exist — the core meaning of the root, consistently rendered with Arabic هَلَكَ (halaka), فَنِيَ (faniya), بَادَ (baada); Korean 멸망하다/멸하다; Swahili kuangamia; Hindi नाश होना/नष्ट होना; covering all Qal inflections (perfect, imperfect, infinitive, cohortative, participle) where the subject undergoes destruction rather than mere displacement.

Qal intransitive sense: to be lost, wander, go astray, disappear — distinguished from 'perish' by Arabic ضَاعَ/ضَائِع/ضَالَّة (lost/straying) and تَائِه (wandering) rather than هَلَكَ (perish); Korean 잃어버린 (lost); Swahili -potea (get lost); Spanish perdido/perdida (lost); English 'lost', 'the lost'; covering Qal participles and finite forms where the subject is displaced or missing rather than dead.

Piel intensive-active sense: to destroy, exterminate, annihilate — the transitive counterpart where an agent actively destroys the object; Arabic أَهْلَكَ (ahlaka, Form IV), أَبَادَ (abaada), إِبَادَة (ibaada); Korean 멸망시키다/파괴하다; Swahili kuangamiza (causative -iza), kuharibu; covering all Piel inflections (perfect, imperfect, infinitive absolute, participle, consecutive).

Hifil causative sense: to cause to perish, bring to destruction — the causative stem where the agent causes the object's destruction; Arabic أُبِيدُ (ubiidu), أُهْلِكُ (uhliku) in causative Form IV patterns; Korean 멸하다/없애다; Swahili kuangamiza; functionally close to Piel but distinguished by causative morphology and occasional Arabic preference for أُبِيدُ over أَهْلَكَ.

Piel sub-sense: to waste, lose, squander — a distinct usage where the object is not violently destroyed but carelessly lost or wasted; Arabic يُضِيعُ (yudii'u, to waste) and لِلْإِضَاعَةِ (for squandering); Korean 잃다 (to lose); Swahili kupoteza (to lose/waste, causative of -potea); Spanish perder (to lose) rather than destruir (to destroy).
